question.problem:
Which of the following products is the LU factorization of a matrix $C?$

I. $C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$

II. $C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]$

III. $C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that in the LU factorization of a matrix $C,$ we write $C=LU$ where the matrix $L$ is a unit lower triangular matrix (a lower triangular matrix that has only $1$'s on the main diagonal) and the matrix $U$ is an upper triangular matrix:

$$
C=\overset{L}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ ∗ & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot \overset{U}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ \\ 0 & ∗\end{aligned}]}}
$$

With that in mind, let's inspect each product in turn.

- The first product is *not* in $LU$ form  because  the matrix on the left is not a unit lower triangular matrix, as its main diagonal contains a number not equal to $1.$

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\,\times 
$$

- The second product is *not* in $LU$ form. Although we have a product of an upper triangular matrix on the left and a unit lower triangular matrix on the right, the order of multiplication is not correct (instead, we need a unit lower triangular matrix on the left and an upper triangular matrix on the right).

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\,\times 
$$

- The third product is in $LU$ form because the left matrix is a unit lower triangular matrix, and the right matrix is an upper triangular matrix. 

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]\,✓
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only".
